title: Lab 3 — Quiz 2
subtitle: Bacterial Growth — TSI, phenol red fermentation, probiotic counts

questions.prompt: Read this TSI tube. What does it show?

options.text: No fermentation (entire medium red)
Ferments glucose only
Ferments glucose and lactose and/or sucrose
H2S production

questions.explanation: Entire medium red: the organism doesn't ferment any of the sugars and doesn't reduce sulfur. Slant −, butt −.

why.B: Glucose-only shows a red slant over a yellow butt.
why.D: H2S shows as a black precipitate.

questions.prompt: Read this TSI tube. What does it show?

options.text: Ferments glucose only
No fermentation
Ferments glucose and lactose and/or sucrose
Reduces sulfur to H2S

questions.explanation: Red slant + yellow butt: the organism ferments glucose only. Slant −, butt +, no cracks, no H2S.

why.B: No fermentation leaves the entire tube red.
why.C: That turns the slant yellow too.
why.D: H2S shows as a black precipitate.

questions.prompt: Read this TSI tube. What does it show?

options.text: Ferments glucose and lactose and/or sucrose, and produces gas
Ferments glucose only and does not produce any gas
Does not ferment any of the sugars but produces gas
Reduces sulfur to H2S and does not ferment any sugar

questions.explanation: Entire medium yellow = ferments glucose and lactose and/or sucrose. Large cracks/gaps = gas was produced.

why.B: Glucose-only fermenters have a red slant.
why.C: Yellow means acid from fermentation; there's no 'no fermentation with gas' result.

questions.prompt: Read this TSI tube. What does the black color mean?

options.text: The organism produced gas from fermentation
The organism does not ferment any sugar
The medium is contaminated and should be discarded
The organism reduced sulfur into hydrogen sulfide (H2S)

questions.explanation: A black precipitate means sulfur was reduced to H2S. In the slide example, it also ferments glucose (slant −, butt +).

why.A: Gas shows as cracks or gaps, not black color.
why.B: No fermentation turns the entire tube red.
why.C: Black precipitate is a positive H2S result.

questions.prompt: In TSI, what do large cracks or gaps in the agar indicate?

options.text: Gas was produced during fermentation
Hydrogen sulfide was produced
The organism is a non-fermenter
The slant was stabbed too deeply

questions.explanation: Cracks or gaps = gas produced during fermentation of any sugar.

why.B: H2S shows as a black precipitate.
why.C: Cracks come from gas made during fermentation.
why.D: Cracks are a gas result, not a technique error.

questions.prompt: How is a TSI slant inoculated?

options.text: Streak only the slant surface using an inoculating loop
Pipette 50 µL onto the slant and spread it
Add a Durham tube and then shake it to mix
Stab top to bottom with an inoculating needle, then streak the slant surface

questions.explanation: Stab the slant from top to bottom with an inoculating needle, then streak the surface. Incubate at 37°C for 24–48 hours.

why.A: TSI is stabbed with a needle and then streaked.
why.B: Spreading 50 µL is the spread plate method.
why.C: Durham tubes go in phenol red broths, not TSI.

questions.prompt: This phenol red broth is yellow and has a bubble in the Durham tube. What is the result?

options.text: Ferments the sugar and produces gas
Ferments the sugar, but no gas
Does not ferment the sugar
Reduces sulfur to H2S

questions.explanation: Phenol red turns yellow (acidic) when the sugar is fermented. The inverted Durham tube traps any gas produced.

why.B: A bubble in the Durham tube means gas was produced.
why.C: Yellow means acid was produced — a positive fermentation.
why.D: Phenol red broth doesn't test H2S.

questions.prompt: This phenol red broth is yellow with no bubble in the Durham tube. What is the result?

options.text: Ferments the sugar and produces gas
Does not ferment the sugar
The test is invalid without a bubble
Ferments the sugar, no gas

questions.explanation: Yellow = positive fermentation. An empty Durham tube = no gas.

why.A: There is no bubble trapped in the Durham tube.
why.B: Yellow means the sugar was fermented to acid.
why.C: A yellow broth with no bubble is a valid result.

questions.prompt: This phenol red broth stayed red-orange. What is the result?

options.text: Ferments the sugar, no gas
Ferments the sugar and produces gas
Does not ferment the sugar
Positive for acid production

why.B: There's no yellow color or trapped bubble.
why.D: Acid would turn phenol red yellow.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the small inverted Durham tube in a phenol red carbohydrate broth?

options.text: To detect acid produced during fermentation
To create an oxygen gradient
To detect gas produced during fermentation
To keep the broth sterile

questions.explanation: The Durham tube traps gas; phenol red shows acid (yellow).

why.A: Phenol red (the pH indicator) detects acid.
why.B: Thioglycolate broth creates an O2 gradient.
why.D: The Durham tube traps gas bubbles.

questions.prompt: Phenol red is used in fermentation tests because it is a:

options.text: Sugar that bacteria break down for energy
Dye that stains bacterial cell walls red
pH indicator that turns black with H2S
pH indicator that turns yellow when acid is produced

questions.explanation: Phenol red: yellow (acidic) at low pH, red-orange near neutral, pink at basic pH.

why.A: Phenol red is a pH indicator, not a sugar.
why.B: It indicates pH; it doesn't stain cells.
why.C: Black in TSI comes from H2S, not from phenol red.

questions.prompt: In fermentation, what is the purpose of Step 2 (reducing pyruvate)?

options.text: To regenerate NAD so glycolysis can continue
To generate most of the cell's ATP
To oxidize glucose into pyruvate
To consume oxygen as the final electron acceptor

questions.explanation: Step 1 (glycolysis) oxidizes glucose and nets 2 ATP. Step 2 reduces pyruvate to acid or alcohol, regenerating NAD.

questions.prompt: The acidity of yogurt, sour cream and sourdough comes from:

options.text: Ethanol fermentation
Hydrogen sulfide production
Aerobic respiration
Lactic acid fermentation

questions.explanation: Lactic acid fermentation (pyruvate reduced to lactic acid) makes yogurt, sour cream and sourdough acidic, and happens in muscles when O2 runs out.

why.A: Ethanol fermentation produces alcohol and CO2.
why.B: H2S is the sulfur result in TSI.
why.C: These foods are acidified by lactic acid fermentation.

questions.prompt: In the probiotic experiment, 100 µL is transferred into 900 µL of water at each step (OG → A → B → C → D). What is the total dilution of Tube D?

why.B: Dilution factors are multiplied, not added.
why.D: Only four 1/10 dilutions were made: A, B, C, D.

questions.prompt: Plate D (total dilution 1/10,000, 50 µL plated) has 45 colonies. How many CFU/mL were in the probiotic?

options.text: 22,500 CFU/mL

why.A: That forgets to divide by the 0.05 mL plated.
why.C: Volume plated goes in the denominator: 45 × 10,000 ÷ 0.05.
